findings.title: DMARC not enforced (p=none): domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud
findings.deal_impact: Domain can be spoofed without enforcement, increasing BEC and wire-fraud risk for fleet customers and finance processes; require DMARC enforcement plan pre-close.

remediation.summary: Move DMARC from p=none through quarantine to reject, monitoring rua reports and aligning SPF/DKIM senders.

findings.title: SPF uses soft/neutral fail
findings.deal_impact: Softfail weakens spoofing protection and compounds the DMARC p=none exposure, raising phishing and invoice-fraud risk.

remediation.summary: Audit authorized senders then change SPF ~all to -all in coordination with DMARC enforcement.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled
findings.deal_impact: Unsigned DNS leaves resolution less protected against spoofing; low direct deal risk but relevant to platform trust and hardening backlog.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC at registrar/DNS provider and validate DS publication and resolver handling.

findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems
findings.deal_impact: Public CT names suggest VPN, legacy Jenkins, staging API, and legacy portal attack surface that may expand diligence scope and remediation backlog.

remediation.summary: Verify ownership and exposure of each risky hostname, restrict access, patch or decommission legacy/staging systems.

findings.title: Large certificate footprint relative to company size
findings.deal_impact: A 47-hostname certificate footprint for a 201-1000 employee SaaS suggests asset sprawl that may complicate inventory, patching, and attack-surface reduction.

remediation.summary: Build authoritative external asset inventory, remove stale certificates/hosts, and enforce issuance approval.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS versions offered

evidence.excerpt: tls_support: TLSv1.0 true, TLSv1.1 true, TLSv1.2 true; tls_versions: TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2

findings.deal_impact: Deprecated TLS on www increases interception/downgrade risk and may conflict with customer security requirements for a fleet telematics platform.

remediation.summary: Disable TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1 at the web tier/load balancer and retain only modern TLS versions.

findings.title: HSTS not set
findings.deal_impact: Without HSTS, users may be downgraded to insecure connections; low standalone risk but an easy hardening and customer-trust gap.

remediation.summary: Set Strict-Transport-Security on apex and www after confirming HTTPS coverage, then consider preload.

findings.title: Internet-facing appliance listed in CISA KEV (version not verified)

evidence.excerpt: CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001; vendor: ExampleGate; product: ExampleGate SSL-VPN; matched fingerprint version 7.0.11; match_tier: appliance_exposed; KEV lists products, not affected versions; version not verified.

findings.deal_impact: Potential exposure: an internet-facing appliance fingerprint matches CISA KEV at product level, with version not verified, creating potential critical perimeter risk pending patch-level confirmation.

remediation.summary: Immediately verify appliance version and patch status against the KEV entry, patch or restrict access, and review logs for exploitation.

findings.title: Publicly disclosed security incident in the last 24 months

evidence.excerpt: type: state_ag_breach_notice; date: 2025-08-14; Notice filed for unauthorized access to a customer support system; approx. 3,100 individuals notified; disclosed_within_months: 14

findings.deal_impact: A 2025 breach notice affecting about 3,100 individuals raises regulatory, customer-notification, retention, and cyber-insurance diligence risk within the last 24 months.

remediation.summary: Diligence incident root cause, remediation evidence, notifications, litigation/regulatory status, and corrective controls; obtain incident reports.

findings.title: Critical subservice organization carved out of SOC 2 scope

evidence.locator: Section 1 — Independent Service Auditor's Report, Subservice organizations; Section 3.2 Infrastructure
evidence.excerpt: Nimbus Cloud Services is carved out of scope: infrastructure hosting.

findings.deal_impact: Nimbus Cloud Services (infrastructure hosting) is carved out of scope and is critical to production or in-scope data.

remediation.summary: Obtain the Nimbus Cloud Services SOC report and assess carve-out risk.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Every admin account is behind MFA. No exceptions. That's been true for years. It's enforced through our conditional access policy.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 testing found 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA, bypassing conditional access via a legacy provisioning script.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Offboarding is automated. HR flags the termination and access is revoked same day through our identity provider.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 testing found 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days, not same-day revocation.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We have a 24 7 SOC through our MSSP, every alert gets looked at, nothing sits.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 exception: for Nov 10-23, 2025, alerts went to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We're fully locked down there. DMARC is enforced. Nobody can spoof our domain.

contradictions.explanation: DMARC record is p=none (monitoring only, not enforced), so spoofing is not blocked.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: No, nothing material. We've never had a breach.

contradictions.explanation: State AG breach notice 2025-08-14 reports unauthorized access to a customer support system, ~3,100 individuals notified.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We decommissioned the legacy stuff a while back. Everything external goes through the main app and the VPN.

contradictions.explanation: CT log presence alone doesn't prove a host is live; however, legacy-portal (last_seen 2026-07-22) and jenkins-old (2026-08-14) certs within the last 12 months show those systems are still actively maintained, contradicting decommissioning.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Annual third party test. The last one came back clean. No highs.

contradictions.explanation: Annual pen test control had no exceptions, but the test reported 2 high-severity findings, contradicting 'clean, no highs'.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Daily backups to immutable storage in a second region and we do a restore test every quarter.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 control A1.2-01 (daily backups to immutable storage, quarterly restore tests) was tested with no exceptions noted.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We can get one. one we haven't needed it so far.

contradictions.explanation: No bridge letter was provided and the report period ended 2026-03-31, but management states it plans to obtain a bridge letter covering Apr 1, 2026 forward upon request, corroborating it can be obtained.

deal_recommendations.text: Require, before signing, verification of the appliance version and patch status, a compromise assessment including review of exploitation logs, and a bring-down of security representations, completing the Days 0–30 actions [F-008].

Authorize an expanded review that independently validates the perimeter exposure and tests management representations against underlying evidence, beginning with the Days 0–30 verification work [F-008].
Negotiate protection for losses arising from the pre-closing disclosed incident, informed by diligence of root cause, notifications and corrective controls in Days 31–60 [F-009].

Confirm with brokers that the known disclosed incident is likely excluded from representation and warranty coverage and reflect any gap in transaction protections, alongside the Days 31–60 incident diligence [F-009].
Engage underwriters early to confirm insurability before close, evidencing planned remediation of domain authentication and administrative access controls in Days 31–60 [F-001] [F-010] [F-011].

Bind the company to a post-close remediation programme covering access enforcement, offboarding, monitoring, change control, email authentication, external exposures and incident corrective actions, sequenced through Days 31–60, Days 61–100 and After day 100 where applicable [F-010] [F-011] [F-012] [F-013] [F-001] [F-002] [F-004] [F-006] [F-009] [F-014].

Record that no price adjustment is warranted on cyber remediation alone, as the $142K–$643K plan, sequenced across Days 0–30 through After day 100, is immaterial relative to the 50M-250M revenue band [F-001] [F-002] [F-003] [F-004] [F-005] [F-006] [F-007] [F-008] [F-009] [F-010] [F-011] [F-012] [F-013] [F-014] [F-015].

narrative.executive_summary: Bottom line: Escalate: full cyber diligence required before signing. The rating is D at 56.8 because caps apply for a critical, potentially exploitable exposure, a publicly disclosed incident within 24 months, and multiple management statements contradicted by evidence [F-008] [F-009] [C-005]. Key risks: A critical perimeter exposure remains unverified at version level. Identity, offboarding and monitoring exceptions weaken access and detection controls. Domain spoofing protection is not enforced. A disclosed incident creates regulatory, customer and insurance exposure [F-008] [F-010] [F-011] [F-012] [F-001] [F-009]. Management credibility: Of 9 claims assessed, 7 were contradicted, 0 unsupported, 2 supported. Management credibility is materially weakened because core claims on access, monitoring, domain protection and incident history were contradicted by independent evidence [C-001] [C-002] [C-003] [C-004] [C-005] [C-006] [C-007]. Next steps: Complete full diligence before signing, verify the critical exposure and any compromise, review the disclosed incident in depth, and validate identity, monitoring and assurance evidence [F-008] [F-009] [F-010] [F-012] [F-014].
key_questions_for_management: Provide evidence of the appliance version, current patch status and completed log review for signs of exploitation [F-008]?
Provide incident reports, root-cause analysis, notification records and the current regulatory and litigation status for the disclosed incident [F-009]?
Reconcile the sampled administrative accounts without enforced multifactor authentication with current access-control records and remediation evidence [F-010] [C-001]?
Reconcile terminated-user records with access revocation timestamps and provide evidence of current offboarding controls [F-011] [C-002]?
Provide evidence that security alerts are now routed, reviewed and escalated without interruption [F-012] [C-003]?
Confirm the plan and timetable for moving domain authentication from monitoring to enforcement and tightening sender policy [F-001] [F-002] [C-004]?
Provide a bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30 and the infrastructure hosting provider assurance report for review [F-014] [F-015]?
